241479387.summary: Six sharp raw SAP eclipses recur over 114 cycles, including adjacent selected-kind cycles 65/66/67. The eclipse and clock are secure. A close capable Gaia neighbor remains unresolved by the target-centered pixel deficit, so ownership remains probable.
241479387.epoch_kind: selected repeating eclipse; primary/secondary identity unestablished
241479387.kinds: All six accepted events use the same selected deep morphology. The full raw diagnostic fold establishes no comparable second eclipse; no upper limit on a shallower other-kind eclipse is claimed. Adjacent s 65 events and actual half-phase nulls test recurrence. The epoch does not claim to name the deeper primary.
241479387.reduction: An independent custom TESScut extraction of the s 102 event at BTJD 4128.98299 reproduces the loss: central 1 x 1,3 x 3,5 x 5 apertures give 40.384,40.446,25.312 ppt. The alternative reduction is deliberately compared by its own diluted depth, not forced to the 51.875 ppt QLP median.
241479387.attribution: The s 102 difference image is concentrated at the target; its positive-deficit centroid offset is 0.139 pixel, descriptive only. The 60 arcsec Gaia census contains 71 sources. Two non-target sources remain capable under optimistic G-band full-capture assumptions at the minimum measured 25.312 ppt aperture loss: Gaia 6070540006339062784 at 8.588 arcsec (about 0.409 TESS pixel), requiring 18.85% intrinsic loss, and Gaia 6070539967673962240 at 41.794 arcsec (about 1.990 pixel), requiring 15.77%. The close neighbor cannot be cleanly separated by this broad pixel deficit. A target-like peak alone does not exclude that neighbor. Source attribution remains unresolved.
241479387.geometry: The period and conjunction differences are approximately 2.07 and 1.99 quoted/linear Gaia sigma respectively: mild tension is retained explicitly, with no exact orbit agreement imposed. This is not a decisive contradiction to the same spectroscopic binary; future velocities could test it.
241479387.limitations: The event is real and repeats, but a capable 8.59 arcsec Gaia neighbor prevents definitive target ownership. Aperture dilution varies strongly, and TIC 241479387 has mild roughly 2 sigma Gaia period/conjunction tension. Timing fit errors are conditional and exclude extraction/model systematics. No exhaustive all-sector characterization or Monte Carlo was performed. Novelty remains pending because scoped catalogue coverage is incomplete.
241479387.next_check: Obtain resolved eclipse photometry separating the 8.59 arcsec neighbor, and compare a new timed eclipse or velocities with the Gaia orbit.

421331604.summary: Five accepted deeper-eclipse midpoints establish the 22.69233-day clock, with many additional clean covered raw events. A shallower other-kind eclipse repeats at phase 0.2876. The independent extraction and target-like difference image, absence of capable nearby Gaia sources, and Gaia geometry support the selected star as an eclipsing spectroscopic binary.
421331604.epoch_kind: deeper selected eclipse; shallower conjunction at phase 0.28756
421331604.kinds: A distinct shallower eclipse is separately measured in five raw events: s14, s54, two s76 events, and s83, with central losses 8.863–9.521 ppt and phases 0.287465–0.287692. These other-kind events are excluded from the deeper-eclipse ephemeris. Their separate table and plots are in opposite-eclipse-kind.json and opposite-eclipse-kind.png. The s 26 deeper event covers only egress and is excluded from precision timing and median depth.
421331604.reduction: Independent custom TESScut extraction of the s 14 deeper event at BTJD 1705.35681 reproduces the loss: central 1 x 1,3 x 3,5 x 5 apertures give 63.759,61.550,58.485 ppt. QLP alternative aperture depths 61.576/70.331/73.799 ppt test additional dilution but are not another pipeline; the custom pixel reduction supplies the independent extraction check.
421331604.attribution: The s 14 difference image follows the target-shaped pixel illumination, with a descriptive positive-deficit centroid offset 0.560 pixel. The target lies near a pixel boundary, so this scalar offset is not a calibrated source probability. All 25 Gaia sources within 60 arcsec were screened at the conservative minimum 58.485 ppt aperture loss; no non-target source is capable under optimistic G-band full-capture assumptions. The target-like deficit and the neighbor census support target attribution at this bounded review level.
421331604.geometry: The period difference is 0.286 quoted Gaia sigma and selected-conjunction offset is 0.183 linear covariance sigma. The separate shallower eclipse nearphase 0.2876 is also consistent with the expected eccentric two-conjunction geometry. No physical contradiction is found.
421331604.limitations: The sector 26 egress-only model is excluded from adopted timing and depth. Depths depend on aperture dilution. Pixel centroids and Gaia G-band capability proxies are descriptive rather than calibrated TESS PRF likelihoods. Timing fit errors exclude model/pipeline systematics. No exhaustive all-sector characterization or Monte Carlo was performed. Physical confirmation is separate from pending catalogue novelty.
421331604.next_check: Recover the missing scoped catalogue checks before any new-system claim; a future clean deeper eclipse can refine the selected-kind clock.
